notes: LuckyJ breaks the 6s 6s 6s 8s block by cutting 8s; Nishiki preserves that shape by cutting 4m.

guide.caption: LuckyJ 8s, Nishiki 4m
guide.situation: South 3-0, middle hand, 26 tiles left. LuckyJ has 35300 points (lead), currently 1st. After drawing [[8s]], LuckyJ cuts [[8s]]; Nishiki's top line is [[4m]]. Result: draw, self delta +1500
guide.read: On 35300 points and currently 1st, this hand does not need to chase extra points. LuckyJ lets it become a controlled fold unless the next draw makes pushing clearly worth it. With the corrected bars, Nishiki's candidate is the hotter tile: [[8s]] has a peak NAGA danger proxy of 4.1%; [[4m]] has a peak NAGA danger proxy of 12.7%. LuckyJ is not simply paying more danger here; it is avoiding that hotter candidate while preserving a different job. The kept [[4m]] is genbutsu against the right player (no called threat). Hibakari also chooses [[8s]], so read this as LuckyJ/Hibakari versus Nishiki, not LuckyJ against every NAGA head.
guide.whyNot: The Nishiki line through [[4m]] is the efficiency temptation because it leaves 0-shanten, 5 visible ukeire, main accepts [[7s]], [[8s]]. LuckyJ's [[8s]] line leaves 0-shanten, 2 visible ukeire, main accepts [[4m]]. That extra acceptance matters less when the score job is to protect the current position, not manufacture more points. LuckyJ lowers the NAGA danger proxy: LuckyJ 4.1%, Nishiki 12.7%.
guide.copy: Copy the score job: when your position is already good enough, lower the ambition, keep safe tiles, and let the hand fold unless a later draw makes it worth pushing.
guide.limit: Do not copy the fold posture when you actually need points, when the hand is already worth pushing, or when the safer line has no real safe tile.
guide.prompt: With 26 tiles left, would you cut [[8s]] or [[4m]]? First say whether you need more points or can protect the current position.
guide.answer: LuckyJ chooses [[8s]]. The reproducible reason is: On 35300 points and currently 1st, this hand does not need to chase extra points. LuckyJ lets it become a controlled fold unless the next draw makes pushing clearly worth it.

guide_ja.caption: LuckyJ 8s、ニシキ 4m
guide_ja.situation: South 3-0、middle、残り26枚。lead、35300点、現在1着。LuckyJ は [[8s]] ツモから [[8s]] を切り、ニシキ第一候補は [[4m]]。結果: draw, self delta +1500
guide_ja.read: 35300点で 現在1着 なので、加点を追いすぎる局面ではない。次のツモで押す価値がはっきり出なければ、LuckyJ はこの手を無理せず降りやすい形へ寄せている。 修正後の脅威バーではニシキ候補の方が熱い。[[8s]] のNAGA最大脅威指標 4.1%、[[4m]] のNAGA最大脅威指標 12.7%。LuckyJ は単に危険を払っているのではなく、熱い候補を避けながら別の価値を残している。 残る [[4m]] は 下家 に対して現物で、相手の状態は静かな相手。 ヒバカリも [[8s]] を第一候補にしており、この例は LuckyJ/ヒバカリ対ニシキの分岐として読む。
guide_ja.whyNot: ニシキの [[4m]] は 0シャンテン、見えている受け入れ5枚、主な受け [[7s]], [[8s]] を残すので、効率面では魅力がある。LuckyJ の [[8s]] は 0シャンテン、見えている受け入れ2枚、主な受け [[4m]]。ただしこの点数状況では、加点を作ることより今の着順を守ることが先に来る。LuckyJ はNAGA危険度指標を下げている。LuckyJ 4.1%、ニシキ 12.7%。
guide_ja.copy: 点数状況を真似する。今の着順を守れば十分なら、目標を下げて安全牌を残し、次のツモで押す価値が出るまで無理しない。
guide_ja.limit: 加点が必要な時、すでに押す価値がある手、または安全牌のない安全寄せでは真似しない。
guide_ja.prompt: 残り26枚で [[8s]] と [[4m]] のどちらを切るか。先に加点が必要か、今の着順を守れば十分かを言う。
guide_ja.answer: LuckyJ は [[8s]] を選ぶ。理由は 35300点で 現在1着 なので、加点を追いすぎる局面ではない。次のツモで押す価値がはっきり出なければ、LuckyJ はこの手を無理せず降りやすい形へ寄せている。

guide.caption: LuckyJ North, Nishiki West

Discarding [[N]] leaves the hand at four-shanten with 82 ukeire, keeping the Chun pair [[C]] as a potential yakuhai engine. Nishiki's preference for discarding [[W]] keeps a slightly different safety profile, but Mortal independently backs LuckyJ's choice of [[N]] at 49%. Releasing this guest wind early prevents it from becoming a dangerous seat-wind value tile for Kamicha once their hands develop. In a high-lead dealer game, release potential opponent value winds early while your own hand is still too slow to fight.

LuckyJ's [[N]] line leaves 4-shanten, 82 visible ukeire, main accepts [[2m]], [[3m]], [[4m]], [[5m]], [[6m]]. That extra acceptance matters less when the score job is to protect the current position, not manufacture more points. The NAGA danger-proxy values are close: LuckyJ 0.1%, Nishiki 0.1%.

guide.caption: LuckyJ 5s, Nishiki 9s
guide.situation: East 1-1, late hand, 13 tiles left. LuckyJ has 26500 points (above starting score), currently 1st. After drawing [[9s]], LuckyJ cuts [[5s]]; Nishiki's top line is [[9s]]. Result: draw, self delta -1000
guide.read: With only 13 tiles remaining in the wall and a dealer hand stuck at 2-shanten, holding onto [[5s]] for wider ukeire is a luxury we can no longer afford. Nishiki's discard of [[9s]] preserves the [[2s]][[3s]][[4s]][[5s]] shape to keep 25 ukeire, but it forces us to hold the middle tile [[5s]], which will become a dangerous liability in the final turns. LuckyJ discards the [[5s]] now while it is still relatively safe—suji to the riichi and genbutsu to shimocha—leaving the terminal [[9s]] as an ironclad safety valve in hand.
